Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order in which numbers are added can affect the result due to rounding errors. Different summation orders may lead to different intermediate results, and the final rounding at each step can produce distinct outcomes. This behavior is a consequence of the finite precision and the specific rounding rules applied in floating-point arithmetic.

This behavior is a consequence of the finite precision and the specific rounding rules used in floating-point arithmetic.
